name: Long runs after p^2 with no prime factor exceeding p (p <= 10^9)
description: construct() -> {'p': p, 'k': k} with p a prime at most 10^9 and 1 <= k <= 200; every integer p^2 + 1, ..., p^2 + k must have all prime factors at most p (exact factorization by trial division and Pollard-Brent with deterministic Miller-Rabin). Maximize k. Long runs for p <= 10^9 are finite evidence for the conjectured positive answer.

sources.locator: Paul Erdős and Ronald L. Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory (1980). Erdős-Graham monograph (L'Enseignement Mathématique, 1980; source of the problem) located. Erdős Problem #383 page inspected: heuristically n has no prime factor >= n^(1/2) with probability 1 - log 2, so a positive answer is expected; it would settle part of #382. No finite values are documented. Long runs for p <= 10^9 are finite evidence for the conjectured positive answer.
